messages:
Jordan (Eng): Heads upplanning a 10-week remote work stretch in Portugal starting mid-June. Ill remain on US payroll. Quick Qs: do I still get the WFH stipend while temporarily abroad? Any company-level tax/nexus concerns if Im roughly 70% in Lisbon over that period? Also want to ship my standing desk there  is that reimbursable?

Anya (People Ops): Congrats! Short answers: youre eligible for a prorated WFH stipend while on a temporary remote stint. Shipping can be reimbursed but needs pre-approval from People Ops for >$500. Please submit the temporary-remote/hub form with dates, % time abroad, hardware list, and manager sign-off. :+1:

Jordan (Eng): What exactly needs to be on the form and who signs it?

Anya (People Ops): The form requests: start/end dates, destination city/country, estimated % time outside homebase, list of items to ship, shipping estimate, and manager acknowledgement. People Ops reviews and Legal gets looped if duration or activities raise flags. Manager signoff is required before we process any shipping reimbursement.

Jordan (Eng): Is there a duration threshold that triggers payroll/localization?

Liam (Payroll): From payroll side: any stay >= 90 days will usually auto-trigger localization workflow (we may switch payroll to local entity, withholdings, etc.). Sub-90 stays generally stay on US payroll but Legal review can change that. If you remain on US payroll we can continue paying the stipend in USD.

Sanjay (Legal): Legal note: personal tax/residency rules (e.g., 183-day rule) are the primary concern for the individual. Company nexus/PE risk for a single headcount on a short trip is low, but depends on location, customer meetings, and whether youre effectively setting up a place of business. At ~70% over 10 weeks (70 days) we typically dont see corporate nexus, but well run a quick jurisdiction check. Please mark the submission as "temporary remote" so Legal can triage. :mag:

Jordan (Eng): For the stipend amount  is it the normal $100/mo prorated or different overseas? Any caps on shipping reimbursement?

Anya (People Ops): If your homebase is still US you receive the standard stipend prorated by days in the month. Shipping receipts required; pre-approval needed for >$500. I can pre-approve up to $600 for desk shipping if you attach quotes.

Liam (Payroll): Also note: if Legal recommends localization, payroll transitions can delay stipend payments and affect tax withholding. Keep your W-9/W-8 info updated if your residency changes.

PeopleOps Bot: Temporary remote form: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/temp-remote-form
Policy summary: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/policies/temp-remote
Automation note: duration >= 90 days -> triggers payroll/localization workflow.

Jordan (Eng): Filing the form now and will add detailed dates (7 weeks Lisbon, 3 weeks back in US inside the 10-week window). Ill DM @Anya shipping quotes and get manager sign-off.

Anya (People Ops): Great  once submitted well tag it "short-term EU" and run Legal + Payroll checks. Expect an update within 48-72 business hours. Ill pre-approve desk shipping up to $600 upon receipt of quotes/manager signoff. :sparkles:

Sanjay (Legal): Well review within 48 hours after form submission. If anything looks like potential nexus, PE, or dependent contractor exposure well flag it and reach out for more info. Portugal specifics: residency typically at 183 days; company risk low for single short trips but well confirm.

Jordan (Eng): Thanks all. Filing now.

PeopleOps Bot: Form received: TR-2026-0783. Next steps: manager signoff -> People Ops review -> Legal/Payroll as needed. ETA: 48-72 hrs.
